title: APPROVAL OF MASTER JOINT REVOCABLE PERMIT NO. 26-14 AMONG VERDANTAS INC. AND CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND PORT OF LONG BEACH, AS JOINT OWNERS
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF MASTER JOINT REVOCABLE PERMIT NO. 26-14 AMONG VERDANTAS INC. AND CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND PORT OF LONG BEACH, AS JOINT OWNERS
Transmittal 1
Transmittal 2
Summary
: Staff requests approval of Master Joint Revocable Permit No. 26-14 (MJRP) among Verdantas Inc. (Verdantas), a California corporation, the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department), and the Port of Long Beach (POLB) as joint owners (collectively Ports), for installation, maintenance, operation and removal of thirty-six CO2 trap, soil gas, and groundwater monitoring facilities at the southwest and southeast corners of E. Opp Street and Farragut Avenue in Wilmington, California. Under the proposed MJRP, Verdantas will be allowed to use an area totaling approximately 5,400 square feet within the Ports’ property for the purpose of installing, operating, maintaining and removing CO2 trap, soil gas monitoring, and groundwater monitoring stations. There will be no rent charged for this MJRP as the permit area will be used in alignment with a separate contract between the Ports and Verdantas to support the Ports’ environmental compliance with water and air monitoring requirements of local and state environmental regulatory agencies, and the overall impact on other uses of the property is negligible. This MJRP requires approval from the Board of Harbor Commissioners of both Ports. The POLB Board of Harbor Commissioners is expected to approve this MJRP at its meeting scheduled for December 14, 2026. This permit is in alignment with Strategic Plan Objective 2: An Efficient, Secure and Sustainable Supply Chain.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is categorically exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article III, Classes 3(4), 4(7) and 6(2) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve Master Joint Revocable Permit No. 26-14 among Verdantas Inc., the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department and the Port of Long Beach, as joint owners; 3) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to Master Joint Revocable Permit No. 26-14; and 4) adopt Resolution No.____________.
